description: Use case: the general part of the photovoltaic return calculation, the phrases, the formulas and the data that are the same for every country; the sun intensity per postal code and the electricity prices of a country are in the file pv_yield_<country>.json of that country. The yearly return of one kWp is the PV yield of the place times the value of one kWh: with self-consumption every kWh replaces a kWh bought at the household electricity price, with feed-in every kWh is sold to the grid at the feed-in remuneration, and the expected return mixes both with the share of the yield that the household uses itself. The calc-validation checks the three formulas with one assumed example installation, because a check may only use the values and formulas of its own file.

words.name: irradiation
words.description: the solar energy that reaches one square metre of a surface over a period, e.g. in kWh per m2 and year

words.name: kWp
words.description: kilowatt peak, the nominal power of photovoltaic panels under the standard test conditions of 1000 W per m2 at 25 degree Celsius

words.name: feed-in
words.description: the delivery of self-produced electricity into the public grid

words.name: self-consumption
words.description: the use of self-produced electricity in the own house, which saves the purchase of the same kWh from the grid

words.name: S2
words.description: the second half of a year from July to December, as Eurostat names the semester of the bi-annual price data

triples.name: postal code
triples.description: the number of a post office area that is part of a postal address; the number is qualified as postal code, e.g. 1950 (postal code), because the same number can also be a year, and each postal code is the triple of the qualified number in its country, named with the country code as prefix, e.g. CH-1950

triples.name: country code
triples.description: the two-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code of a country, used as the prefix of its postal codes

triples.name: global horizontal irradiation
triples.description: the direct and the diffuse solar irradiation on a horizontal surface

triples.name: optimal slope
triples.description: the inclination of a fixed panel to the horizontal that gives the highest yearly irradiation at a place

triples.name: irradiation on optimal slope
triples.description: the direct, diffuse and reflected solar irradiation on a panel at the optimal slope and azimuth

triples.name: PV yield
triples.description: the electricity that photovoltaic panels deliver to the grid or the house, after the losses of the cables, the inverter, the temperature and the dirt

triples.name: household electricity price
triples.description: the total price of one kWh for a household: energy, grid usage, metering, taxes and levies

triples.name: feed-in remuneration
triples.description: the price that the grid operator pays for one kWh of electricity fed into the grid

triples.name: PV return
triples.description: the money that photovoltaic panels earn or save per year, either by replacing electricity bought from the grid or by selling electricity to the grid

triples.name: self-consumption share
triples.description: the share of the PV yield that is used in the own house at the time it is produced; the rest is fed into the grid

formulas.name: PV return by self-consumption
formulas.description: the upper bound of the yearly return of one kWp: every kWh of the yield is used in the own house and replaces a kWh bought at the household electricity price

formulas.name: PV return by feed-in
formulas.description: the lower bound of the yearly return of one kWp: every kWh of the yield is fed into the grid and paid with the feed-in remuneration

formulas.name: PV return by self-consumption share
formulas.description: the expected yearly return of one kWp: the self-consumed share of the yield replaces electricity bought at the household electricity price and the rest is fed into the grid and paid with the feed-in remuneration
formulas.expression: "PV return" = "PV yield" * ( "self-consumption share" * "household electricity price" + ( 1 - "self-consumption share" ) * "feed-in remuneration" )

sources.name: PVGIS 5.3
sources.description: Photovoltaic Geographical Information System version 5.3 of the European Commission Joint Research Centre, tool PVcalc queried on 8 October 2026 with the default settings: radiation database PVGIS-SARAH3 with the years 2005 to 2023, meteorological data ERA5, horizon shading calculated from the elevation model, crystalline silicon panels with a peak power of 1 kWp and 14 percent system loss, free-standing at the optimal slope and azimuth for the yield and at slope 0 for the global horizontal irradiation.

sources.name: Eurostat electricity prices for household consumers
sources.description: Eurostat dataset nrg_pc_204, electricity prices for household consumers, bi-annual data, queried on 8 October 2026: the national average price of the consumption band DC (2500 to 4999 kWh per year) including all taxes and levies in EUR per kWh, also for the countries outside the euro area; the second half of 2025 is the latest semester with a price for every country.

sources.name: Kanton Zürich battery storage for a terraced house with PV
sources.description: Canton of Zurich, pilot project energy: Viridén + Partner AG measured a 3.75 kWp photovoltaic installation on the terraced house Nassackerstrasse 29 in Schlieren from July 2014 to September 2017, the first year without battery, then with 5.5 kWh and 11 kWh of battery; the installation produces about 3100 kWh per year, of which only 30 percent are used directly in the house without storage.

values.source: Kanton Zürich battery storage for a terraced house with PV
values.description: measured without battery on a terraced house in Schlieren with 3.75 kWp; a house with a heat pump, an electric car, a battery or a smaller installation uses a larger share itself
